scope: Proposition 8.1 (Projection constraints) of the manuscript “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (preprints/The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 49cc52aa3de89f0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 68-69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At almost every interior point (c, a) where the full-cell thresholds lie in the permitted range, the following assertions hold. In every case write a1 = jX and v1 = jV . If τ ̸= ℓ, write y1 = jY and u1 = jU , where the conditional rates are ordered by increasing speed ki. Each belongs to [0, 1], and a1 ≥ y1, u1 ≥ v1, v1 > 0 =⇒ y1 ≥ min{1, s0 + v1}, a1 < 1 =⇒ u1 ≤ (a1 − s0)+. (8.1) 68 If τ = ℓ, put m1 = j{Y,U}. Then a1, v1 ∈ [0, 1], m1 ∈ [0, 2], and a1 < 1 =⇒ m1 ≤ 1 + (a1 − s0)+, v1 ≤ (a1 − s0)+. (8.2) These conclusions apply on both signs of the offset whenever those offsets are in the permitted range.
